clue.text: Elderly wife stuck in vehicle, creating conflict

indicators.note: stuck in says the elderly-wife letters are lodged inside the vehicle word

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
elderly means old

explanation.surface: An old woman wedged into a car sparks a family row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conflict' looks like a household quarrel in the surface, but it points to the historic East-West standoff.
explanation.definitionFit: The decades-long standoff between the Soviet bloc and the West was a conflict without direct fighting.

clue.text: Two short blokes dance

indicators.note: two says the shortened bloke word appears twice
short means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a chap is a bloke; the plural signals two of them

explanation.surface: A pair of small men take to the dance floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' looks like it describes the blokes' height but it trims CHAP to CHA.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively Latin American ballroom routine is a dance.

clue.text: Smooth section of recital, e.g. at opera

indicators.note: section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A smooth passage in a musical recital, at an opera for example.
explanation.definitionFit: In music the term directs notes played smoothly and connected, without breaks.

clue.text: What sorceress might do with burning ship

parts.note: an itch is a burning desire
a craft is a ship or vessel

explanation.surface: A sorceress sets a vessel alight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'burning' suggests flames, but it is the desire sense, giving ITCH.
explanation.definitionFit: Casting spells and practising magic is the activity a sorceress engages in.

clue.text: River also rising, trapping small perch

indicators.note: trapping means the rising also word holds the small letter
in a down clue, rising means the also word reads upwards

parts.note: too means also

explanation.surface: A river also swelling, catching small freshwater fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perch' looks like the fish, but it is the bird's resting place; 'rising' turns TOO into OOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar or branch where a bird settles to sleep is a perch.

clue.text: Shorten a game

parts.note: bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: Someone wants to cut a game short.
explanation.definitionFit: To abridge a text is to cut it down, a direct synonym for making it shorter.

clue.text: A wobbly Israeli on top of trapeze?

definitions.text: A wobbly Israeli on top of trapeze?

indicators.note: wobbly suggests unsteadiness, so these letters are jumbled
top of picks the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: An Israeli performer teeters atop a circus trapeze.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue both builds the answer and describes it: a wobbly figure on a trapeze.
explanation.definitionFit: A circus acrobat who performs high above the ground, as on a trapeze, fits the picture.

clue.text: Regretted vulgar broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means sent out on air, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: rude means vulgar

explanation.surface: Someone was sorry for an offensive transmission.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling sorry about something you did is to have regretted it.

clue.text: Bird and dog unite

parts.note: a dove is a bird
to dog someone is to follow them, which is to tail them

explanation.surface: A bird and a dog join forces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dog' is a verb meaning follow, giving TAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: To fit together neatly like interlocking joints is to unite or combine.

clue.text: Lay down each narcissus initially on tomb

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letters of the two words before it

parts.note: a shrine can be a tomb or holy burial place

explanation.surface: Lay a daffodil down on each grave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'each' looks like part of the surface's instruction, but its first letter joins N from narcissus; the definition is to lay down as a principle.
explanation.definitionFit: To establish a right firmly, as in law, is to lay it down formally.

clue.text: Try penetrating cunning jargon

indicators.note: penetrating means the word for try goes into the word for cunning

parts.note: art can mean cunning or craft, as in artful
to have a go is to try

explanation.surface: Having a go at cutting through clever jargon.
explanation.definitionFit: Argot is the specialised slang of a group, the same thing as jargon.

clue.text: Harry sure loves US!

indicators.note: to harry is to harass or disturb, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An exclamation that Harry really loves the speakers, perhaps the royal Harry and America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' looks like a name but is the anagram signal; 'US' looks like the United States but is the pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: The reflexive pronoun for the first person plural stands in for 'us' as emphatic object.

clue.text: Children captured by that mean, horrible enforcer

indicators.note: captured by means the children abbreviation is held inside the other letters
horrible suggests something messed up, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Kids taken by a nasty, mean thug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Children' is the dictionary abbreviation CH; 'horrible' is the anagram signal and 'captured by' places those two letters within the rearranged fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A hired heavy who carries out a boss's ruthless orders is an enforcer.

clue.text: Prison disturbance

definitions.meaning: slang for a jail, as in doing time inside

explanation.surface: A riot behind bars.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is British slang for jail and also means a commotion.

clue.text: Pleasing story about a very old upper-class Republican

indicators.note: about means the story word goes around the following letters

parts.note: a fable is a story

explanation.surface: An agreeable tale about an aged posh American politician.
explanation.walkthrough: FABLE opens after F to take in AVOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that gives approval or a good impression is pleasing.

clue.text: Change to a signorina's make-up

indicators.note: change tells us to alter the order of these letters

parts.note: the letters of 'to a signorina' are rearranged; the 's stands for 'is', linking to the definition

explanation.surface: Someone suggests a young Italian woman alter her cosmetics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make-up' looks like cosmetics but means structure; the 's reads as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The way something is arranged or structured, its composition, is its organisation.

clue.text: Escort agency below adult clubs

indicators.note: in a down clue, below means the agency word comes after the adult and clubs letters

parts.note: A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
a company is a business or agency

explanation.surface: An escort agency is listed beneath adult clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Escort agency' reads as one phrase, but 'Escort' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To go along with someone as a companion is to escort them.

clue.text: Rich for life with no European in charge

parts.note: pro means for, as in pros and cons

indicators.note: with no means the European letter is removed from the life word

parts.note: the word itself, taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone backs a life sentence without European oversight.
explanation.definitionFit: Abundant or fruitful, producing plentifully, as rich soil does.

clue.text: Pop singer risque — not cold fish

parts.note: Sting is the British rock and pop singer, former frontman of the Police

indicators.note: not cold means the cold letter is left out

parts.note: racy means risque or suggestive

explanation.surface: A pop star's risque act is not a cold fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cold fish' reads as a phrase for an unemotional person; 'fish' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat cartilaginous sea creature with a barbed tail is a kind of fish.

clue.text: Moving into Africa — it gets approval

indicators.note: moving shifts these letters into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A plan to relocate to Africa is given the go-ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal confirmation of a treaty or decision is approval of it.

clue.text: Street with widespread discord

parts.note: rife means widespread

explanation.surface: A street full of quarrelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Conflict and bitter disagreement amount to discord.

clue.text: Regularly sends in rubbish, upsetting my boss

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the words
in a down clue, upsetting turns the rubbish word upside down

parts.note: rot means rubbish or nonsense

explanation.surface: A setter complains the boss keeps sending in junk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'my boss' is the setter speaking: the person who oversees a crossword setter.
explanation.definitionFit: The person who commissions and checks a setter's puzzles is that setter's superior.

clue.text: Fallen tree trunk around northern pine

indicators.note: around means the fallen trunk word goes about the northern letter

parts.note: a log is a fallen tree trunk

explanation.surface: A felled log lies near a northern pine tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pine' looks like the tree but is the verb to yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: To yearn for something, as in longing for home, is to pine.

clue.text: I'm flipping irritated after one male entered the country

indicators.note: after says the flipped and irritated words follow the one-and-male letters

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: flipping turns the letters of I'm around

parts.note: the contraction gives its letters I and M
grated means annoyed or irritated, as in it grated on me

explanation.surface: An exasperated speaker complains about a man who arrived in the land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' looks like a mild oath but turns IM into MI; IM from 'one male' starts the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who moved to settle permanently in a new land has come into that country.

clue.text: Ne'er-do-well I had left with the Queen

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I had
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A wastrel reports leaving with the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A lazy good-for-nothing who avoids work is a ne'er-do-well.

clue.text: Part of Russia is actually up here?

definitions.text: Part of Russia is actually up here?

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the hidden letters read from bottom to top
part of says the letters are found within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A geography note that much of Russia lies in the region above.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue builds and describes the answer: most of Russia lies east of the Urals, in this continent.
explanation.definitionFit: Russia's vast Siberian territory is part of the largest continent on Earth.

clue.text: Prevent everyone going east of woodland

indicators.note: in an across clue, east is to the right, so the everyone word comes after the woodland word

parts.note: a forest is woodland
all means everyone

explanation.surface: The whole crowd heads east of the woods.
explanation.definitionFit: To act in advance so as to stop something happening is to prevent it.

clue.text: Made bedspread black for queen

indicators.note: black for queen means the black letter replaces the queen letter

parts.note: a quilt is a bedspread
Q is the chess and card abbreviation for queen
B is the pencil abbreviation for black

explanation.surface: A bedspread was dyed black for the queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Something constructed or put together has been made, a past participle synonym.

clue.text: One whinges a lot about railway, darling

parts.note: C, short for circa, means about
baby is a term of endearment like darling

explanation.surface: A sweetheart moans constantly about the train line.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who complains or sulks at every setback, like a weepy infant, is called this.

clue.text: Animal paddled here by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the words are judged by how they are spoken

parts.note: rowed here, said quickly, gives the sound needed

explanation.surface: Someone canoed to this spot to see wildlife.
explanation.definitionFit: A small Eurasian deer species is an example of an animal.
